t:
(a) 
Chaplains.—
So much of section 15 of the National Defense Act, as amended (10 U. S. C. 234), as reads “One chaplain of rank not below that of major may be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, to be Chief of Chaplains. He shall serve as such for four years, and shall have the rank, pay, and allowances of colonel while so serving” is hereby amended to read: “There is authorized a Chief of Chaplains with the rank of major general.”
 
    (b) 
Medical Department.—
So much of section 10 of the National Defense Act, as amended (10 U. S. C. 81), as reads “The Medical Department shall consist of one Surgeon General with the rank of major general, four assistants with the rank of brigadier general, one of whom shall be an officer in the Dental Corps,” is hereby amended to read “The Medical Department shall consist of one Surgeon General with the rank of major general, one assistant with the rank of major general who shall be an officer in the Dental Corps, three assistants with the rank of major general or brigadier general, as determined by the Secretary of War, and”.

fable.w: The section only amends the National Defense Act to change the ranks of the Chief of Chaplains and Medical Department officers. The tempting reading is that "advice and consent of the Senate" or a determination "by the Secretary of War" signals consultation, but the Senate and the Secretary are both inside the federal government, and the Senate language is in the text being replaced. No outside party such as a state, expert, or the public is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: three assistants with the rank of major general or brigadier general, as determined by the Secretary of War

qwen_block.w: This section amends the National Defense Act to change the rank and structure of military departments (Chaplains and Medical Department). It involves only federal officials (the President, Senate, Secretary of War) and military officers, who are all inside the federal government. There is no consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, states, or private organizations.
qwen_block.s: There is authorized a Chief of Chaplains with the rank of major general.

opus.w: The section only changes officer ranks and positions, and the decisions it describes are left to federal officials such as the Secretary of War. The tempting reading treats the 'advice and consent of the Senate' language as consultation, but the Senate is inside the federal government, and that language is being struck out anyway. No state, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: three assistants with the rank of major general or brigadier general, as determined by the Secretary of War, and
opus.b:
This section is about Army officer positions and ranks. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

The tempting reading is that "by and with the advice and consent of the Senate" counts as consultation. It doesn't, for two reasons. First, the Senate is part of the federal government, so its advice and consent is intra-government action. Second, this phrase appears in the text that the amendment deletes, so it doesn't set up any ongoing process. The remaining actors are the President and the Secretary of War, who are also inside the government.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the National Defense Act to change the rank and composition of the Chaplains and Medical Departments within the Army. These are internal federal government matters involving federal employees (military officers). There is no consultation with or participation by outside parties (states, tribes, public, etc.).
qwen_chat.s: So much of section 15 of the National Defense Act, as amended (10 U. S. C. 234), as reads “One chaplain of rank not below that of major may be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, to be Chief of Chaplains. He shall serve as such for four years, and shall have the rank, pay, and allowances of colonel while so serving” is hereby amended to read: “There is authorized a Chief of Chaplains with the rank of major general.”
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves appointments and changes in military structure.
Resolution: This section amends the National Defense Act to change the rank and composition of the Chaplains and Medical Departments within the Army. These are internal federal government matters involving federal employees (military officers). There is no consultation with or participation by outside parties (states, tribes, public, etc.).
